subject: Scheduling: regional demo — recurring invite showing fixed local time
messages:
From: Sofia Vega <sofia@heliosplatform.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 27 Sep 2026 13:04:00 -0700
Subject: [Helios] Request: recurring weekly demo — calendar showing same local time for all

Alex / Marissa —

Thanks for the quick intro today. I created a recurring calendar invite for a weekly technical demo and sent it to our international team. However, folks in our APAC office keep seeing the invite at 09:00 local while US folks see 16:00 local — it looks like the event is "floating" and not anchored to a timezone, which causes confusion when forwarded between Office 365 and Google Calendar.

I attached the original invite (demo-request.ics) — can you confirm which timezone Redwood expects and whether you can send separate regional invites? Our platform team needs stable local times so engineers can book around it.

Attendees: Sofia Vega (Helios, org lead), Peter Lang (Helios, SRE), Mei Tan (APAC QA)
Attachment: demo-request.ics (text/calendar)

Sofia Vega
Platform Partnerships
Helios Platform
sofia@heliosplatform.com

VERSION:2.0

DTSTART:20261004T160000
DTEND:20261004T170000

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Vega <sofia@heliosplatform.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 27 Sep 2026 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [Helios] Request: recurring weekly demo — calendar showing same local time for all

Hi Sofia —

Thanks for flagging this and for the calendar extract. We see this when an event is created without an explicit TZID on the DTSTART/DTEND and then forwarded between different calendar systems — some clients interpret it as a "floating" time. Two quick options to avoid the mismatch: 

1) Send a fresh invite that sets DTSTART/DTEND with a TZID (e.g., Europe/London or UTC) so it anchors correctly across clients.
2) We can create three separate invites (US, EU, APAC) at region-local times so your teams get an invite that never moves.

If you prefer option 2, propose three slots and we'll send the three invites from our side to avoid the forwarding ambiguity. If you prefer one canonical invite, please regenerate the .ics with TZID or we can create the event in Google Calendar and add your attendees (we'll keep a copy for the Helios attendees).

For context I'm looping Marissa (AE) who will coordinate the mutual action plan and logistics. Also happy to add Dylan from Technical Ops if we need to confirm runtime environment or SSO SAML access prep.

Next steps suggestion: can you confirm
- Which slot (local) your APAC team prefers
- Whether you want separate regional invites or a single UTC-anchored invite

Thanks — I can take care of sending the corrected invites once you confirm.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Developer Relations, Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Vega <sofia@heliosplatform.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2026 08:07:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: [Helios] Request: recurring weekly demo — calendar showing same local time for all

Sofia —

Appreciate the heads-up. We recommend separate invites per region for recurring sessions when customers regularly include cross-region attendees — it reduces no-shows and avoids client-specific quirks (Google vs Exchange). 

I attached a short mutual action plan (MAP_Helios_v1.pdf) showing what we'll cover in the first 3 sessions, and proposed slots below (all shown in UTC for clarity):
- US-friendly: Tuesdays 16:00 UTC (Tuesday US late morning)
- EU-friendly: Wednesdays 09:00 UTC (EU morning)
- APAC-friendly: Thursdays 02:00 UTC (APAC morning)

Alex / Dylan: if that's OK, I'll create three separate recurring invites from our Google Calendar and set TZID explicitly for each calendar event (America/Los_Angeles, Europe/London, Asia/Singapore). Dylan, can you confirm capacity for a 30-minute demo + 15 minutes of live Q/A for APAC (we want to route to the nearest runtime region)?

Sofia — if you prefer, we can also send one single invite anchored to UTC and ask attendees to accept which maps to their local time automatically — just note forwarded copies sometimes strip TZID.

Attachment: MAP_Helios_v1.pdf (application/pdf)

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Sofia Vega <sofia@heliosplatform.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Peter Lang <peter@heliosplatform.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2026 10:12:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: [Helios] Request: recurring weekly demo — calendar showing same local time for all

Thanks Marissa / Alex — this is perfect. We'll go with separate regional invites to keep our schedules predictable. APAC would like the Thursday/APAC slot you proposed. Please proceed with creating the three recurring events and include Mei Tan (mei.tan@heliosplatform.com) for APAC QA.

I've regenerated the .ics from our GSuite and attached an updated calendar file (demo-ics-updated.ics) — this one includes TZID=UTC on DTSTART and DTEND and seems to behave when forwarded. We'll accept the EU-friendly slot for our EU engineering managers and the US slot for our US product owners; Mei will accept the APAC invite.

Attachment: demo-ics-updated.ics (text/calendar)

Appreciate the quick coordination. Looking forward to the first session — please include a Google Meet link in each invite.

Best,
Sofia
